h: The Census Opens the Blessings of Shavuos

p: קוֹרִין פָּרָשַׁת בְּמִדְבַּר קוֹדֶם חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת
Parshas Bamidbar is read before the festival of Shavuos,
and this is as stated in Tosafos (Megillah 31b),
Parshas Nitzavim and Vayeilech are divided in two
כְּשֶׁחָל שַׁבָּת בֵּין יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְסוּכּוֹת
when there is a Shabbos between Yom Kippur and Sukkos,
כְּדֵי לְהַפְסִיק קוֹדֶם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּפָרָשַׁת נִצָּבִים
in order to make a break before Rosh HaShanah with Parshas Nitzavim
between the curses of Mishneh Torah
וּכְמוֹ כֵן קוֹרִין פָּרָשַׁת בְּמִדְבַּר קוֹדֶם עֲצֶרֶת
And likewise Parshas Bamidbar is read before Atzeres,
כְּדֵי לְהַפְסִיק בֵּין הַקְּלָלוֹת שֶׁבְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים
in order to make a break between the curses of Toras Kohanim
And seemingly this is not sufficient reason
that it should be necessary specifically
to read Parshas Bamidbar before it;
שֶׁהֲלֹא הַיָּמִים שֶׁבֵּין פָּרָשַׁת בְּחוּקוֹתַי לְהֶחָג
for the days between Parshas Bechukosai and the festival
would themselves also be a break.
in reading the rebukes before Atzeres
so that the year and its curses may end,
as it says (in the Gemara there);
so that the year and its blessings may begin.
וְזֶה דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי קְרִיאַת הַפָּרָשָׁה
And this comes specifically through the reading of the parsha
on the Shabbos before the festival.
For Shabbos is the source of blessings,
"and all the blessings above and below
בְּיוֹמָא שְׁבִיעָאָה תַּלְיָין (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
depend on the seventh day" (Zohar II 88a),
all the six weekdays that follow.
And it is "the first of the holy convocations,"
the holiness of the festivals that come
in the six weekdays after it.
Now the Yom Tov of Atzeres
never occurs, according to our calendar,
but only on one of the six weekdays.
Parshas Bamidbar on the preceding Shabbos,
from which the source of blessing shines forth
that the year and its blessings may begin.
that it falls on Shabbos itself,
עִם כׇּל זֶה הֲלֹא לֹא נִשְׁאַר
רַק שַׁבָּת אַחַת עַל פָּרָשַׁת הַאֲזִינוּ
only one Shabbos for Parshas Ha'azinu,
כְּדֵי לְסַיֵּים הַתּוֹרָה בְּשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה כַּנָּהוּג
so as to complete the Torah on Simchas Torah, as is the custom.
And the matter of the resting of the blessing
specifically through the reading of Parshas Bamidbar:
by understanding why this sefer is called
עַל שֵׁם הַמִּסְפָּר שֶׁל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
after the count of the Bnei Yisrael
הֲלֹא יֵשׁ עוֹד כַּמָּה עִנְיָנִים וּמִצְוֹת
are there not many other matters and mitzvos
But it is in the manner of
שֶׁאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ג, ה)
what is stated in the Midrash Rabbah (Bereishis Rabbah 3:5):
corresponding to the five Chumshei Torah;
וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחוֹשֶׁךְ
"And God separated between the light and the darkness"
שֶׁמַּבְדִּיל בֵּין יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם לְבָאֵי הָאָרֶץ
which separates between those who left Mitzrayim and those who entered the Land.
That is because in this sefer
there is mentioned twice, in detail,
the count of the Bnei Yisrael:
which is the count of those who left Mitzrayim;
and a second count in Parshas Pinchas,
at the division of the Land, for those who entered the Land.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּמִדְבַּר פָּרָשָׁה ב)
And our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash Rabbah (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:11):
once when they went down to Mitzrayim, etc.,
אַחַת בַּדְּגָלִים וְאַחַת בְּחִילּוּק הָאָרֶץ כּוּלֵּי
one at the banners and one at the division of the Land, etc.,
and one in the future to come,
עוֹד תַּעֲבוֹרְנָה הַצֹּאן עַל יְדֵי מוֹנֶה
'The flocks shall again pass under the hands of one who counts them.'"
differ favorably from the other counts,
where only the total number is mentioned:
בְּשִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ יָרְדוּ מִצְרַיְמָה (דְּבָרִים י, כב)
"with seventy souls they went down to Mitzrayim" (Devarim 10:22),
and at the Exodus from Mitzrayim,
כְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אֶלֶף רַגְלִי (שְׁמוֹת יב, לז)
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל וּבִימֵי דָוִד
and likewise in the days of Shaul and the days of David,
only the total number is mentioned.
This is not so with the two counts
all the counts of the tribes
and the families are detailed individually.
And this is because these two counts
are to root in the souls of Yisrael
the source of blessing of the holiness
בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
of the aspect of Torah she'bichsav and Torah she'b'al peh.
The first count, of those who left Mitzrayim,
is the aspect of the holiness of Torah she'bichsav,
And the second count, of those who entered the Land,
which is the generation of Yehoshua,
who brought them into the Land,
הוּא בְּחִינַת קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
is the aspect of the holiness of Torah she'b'al peh.
וְהוּא עִנְיַן פְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה כִּפְנֵי חַמָּה
And this is the matter of "the face of Moshe was like the face of the sun"
that is, the illumination of Torah she'bichsav,
"and the face of Yehoshua like the face of the moon,"
this is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
from the aspect of Torah she'bichsav.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּלְשׁוֹן
And therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, used the expression
"and he handed it over to Yehoshua" (Avos 1:1)
in the bracketed passage from another manuscript,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּהוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם סִימָן ח
and it is also in the Additions there, section 8;
and this is because Torah she'bichsav he handed to the Levi'im,
as stated explicitly in the pasuk;
which is transmitted from mouth to ear;
and as is known, it was then that there began
וְזֶהוּ וַיַּבְדֵּל בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ
And this is "And He separated between the light and the darkness":
between those who left Mitzrayim and those who entered the Land.
For the aspect of Torah she'bichsav
is called light that flows from above,
and Torah she'b'al peh is called darkness,
הָעָם הַהוֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל
"The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light";
and "He has placed me in darkness" (Eichah 3:6)
which serves specifically to illuminate the darkness.
And the main completion of the count
will be in the future to come,
as it says, "The flocks shall again pass
under the hands of one who counts them";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל פְּרָטֵי נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
that is, all the individual souls of Yisrael will be clarified,
that they have a root in the holiness of the Torah,
גַּם מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶסְתֵּר וְהֶעְלֵם
even what was utterly concealed and hidden
and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said,
that all the Torah of this world
הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
is vanity before the Torah of Mashiach

p: And one may also allude in this
to what is mentioned in the Midrash Rabbah (on this parsha, Bamidbar Rabbah 2:12),
that the number of the seed of Yisrael
to the stars of the heavens, to the dust of the earth,
and to the sand of the sea.
that are stated in Chumash HaPekudim, as mentioned above,
and the third in the future to come,
when the count will be utterly complete,
is included in heavens, earth and seas,
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם
"For in six days Hashem made the heavens
and the earth, the sea" etc.
For in the earth is found
the whole of the creation of the heavens,
as stated in the Tikkunim (in the passage Pasach Eliyahu, Tikkunei Zohar Introduction 17a):
"And You created heaven and earth, etc.,
And the seas are the whole
of the creation of heaven and earth,
as is written in the Pesikta,
כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בַּיַּבָּשָׁה יֵשׁ בַּיָּם
that whatever exists on dry land exists in the sea.
Now the aspect of heaven and earth
Torah she'bichsav and Torah she'b'al peh,
as stated in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 66:3):
"'Of the dew of the heavens' — this is Scripture;
'and of the fat places of the earth' — this is Mishnah."
And the count in which they were likened to the stars of the heavens
alludes to the count of the banners,
which was to root in the souls of Yisrael
And "like the dust of the earth"
יְרַמֵּז עַל הַמִּסְפָּר שֶׁל בָּאֵי הָאָרֶץ
alludes to the count of those who entered the Land,
לְהַשְׁרִישׁ בָּהֶם קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
to root in them the holiness of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is from the side of the receivers,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא (דְּבָרִים ל, יב)
as it says, "It is not in heaven" (Devarim 30:12).
And "like the sand of the sea"
alludes to the utter completeness of the count
when there will then be clarified
the ultimate whole of the aspect of Da'as,
כִּי מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה אֶת ה׳
"For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem
as the waters cover the sea";
and this is the aspect of the Torah of Mashiach.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז הַפָּסוּק (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יט–כ)
And to this alludes the pasuk (Mishlei 3:19–20):
that is, the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh;
"by His knowledge the depths were split"
this is the aspect of Da'as
that will be revealed in the future to come,
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קיז, א)
and as stated in the holy Zohar (I 117a)
on the pasuk "On this day were split
all the fountains of the great deep,
and the windows of the heavens" (Bereishis 7:11):
and the springs of wisdom below.
that Torah she'bichsav is rooted in the aspect of Chochmah,
and Torah she'b'al peh in the aspect of Binah,
from His mouth come knowledge and understanding"
regarding the creation of heaven and earth,
that for creation the heavens came first,
and for completion the earth came first.
כְּמוֹ כֵן בְּחָכְמָה יָסַד אָרֶץ דַּיְיקָא
So too, "with wisdom He founded the earth" specifically:
that is, the foundation and the endurance
is through the aspect of Chochmah
the endurance and foundation of Torah she'bichsav
הוּא בִּתְבוּנָה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
is through the understanding of Torah she'b'al peh,
because they are included one in the other.
